name: Demo G11: Move-Like Redline Light
description: Exercise a move-like redline operation using an explicit lighting-fixture modeled family-instance target with strict type, movement-vector, visual-gate, and cleanup evidence.
setup_instructions: Open a disposable Revit model or a model that can be closed without saving.
Use a view, level, and lighting fixture family/type that can be safely placed, moved, and deleted.
If the model lacks a host-compatible lighting type, keep this task out of the local live override until discovery finds one.
success_criteria: A disposable light family instance id is created in the model.
The native create result returns family/type/name evidence matching the requested lighting symbol.
The created light id is visible in the pre-move visible-element inventory with a model-space point.
Native move dry-run and apply evidence include the created light id.
The post-move visible-element inventory contains the same id at the requested model-space delta.
A deterministic move visual gate artifact passes using before/after capture evidence.
The moved light is cleaned up with native dry-run and applied delete effect evidence.
failure_criteria: The light is not created or is created as a different requested type.
The before/after visible-element inventory cannot prove the requested movement vector.
Move dry-run or apply omits the light id from effect evidence.
The move visual gate artifact is missing or fails.
Cleanup delete dry-run/apply omits the light id from effect evidence.
grader_notes: This task makes lighting fixtures a first-class move-like benchmark instead of relying only on the generic family-instance task.
Text-note or tag evidence must not satisfy this task; it requires modeled family-instance proof.
